rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 5 "Shape the target: threshold and count": line 77: 'Pair with **null-case escape** to give *no* somewhere to go.' 'Null-case escape' is not named anywhere in the file up to this point — it is first defined at line 263 (chunk 17, "Shape the boundary: escalation and refusal"), 12 chunks later. This is the rule's own canonical shape of violation: a forward reference, name-dropped before the deck has introduced it. Harm: a reader hitting chunk 5 in a sequential deck read has no idea what 'null-case escape' is; the cross-reference reads as an unresolved pointer, not a payoff, until they reach chunk 17 eleven slides on. Cross-checked every other bolded cross-reference in the file (lines 183 'a body primer' — generic phrase, not a named entry; line 275 'null-case escape' — backward, chunk 18 after chunk 17; all three-move-pattern citations in chunks 22-24 — backward only). This is the sole forward reference found.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either drop the forward name-drop at line 77 and just say 'pair with the refusal move below' (reading-order pointer, not a named jump), or move the two entries so Earnable threshold follows Null-case escape.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 0 "Prompt anatomy: the named moves": line 11: 'Per-entry shape: bold lead-in carrying both definition and the first beat of the why.' chunk 21 "Shape the continuity: the concreteness forcing function": line 307: '**Names the moment, quotes the beat.**' Both use 'beat' — a rule-8-named maintainer-dialect term — as the file's own authorial voice explaining itself directly to the student reader, not as a quoted specimen displaying a rule verbatim and not the 'forcing function' carve-out (which the compendium clears as ordinary AE101 shop vocabulary, distinct from 'beat'). Checked the other 'beat' hits and found them exempt: line 27's *'Read these four beats'* and line 309's *'Quote the specific session beat.'* are both italicised, quotation-marked citations of real prompt text (the file's own stated convention: 'italicised quote from a real Agents 101 or AE101 prompt') — they display what an actual prompt says, they do not use 'beat' as the file's own narration to the reader, so they read as specimens rather than communicated dialect and are not flagged. Harm at lines 11 and 307: an engineer reader with no narrative-jargon background hits 'beat' used as plain description and has to guess what it means.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Line 11: 'first line of the why' or similar. Line 307: 'quotes the moment' (the sentence already uses 'moment' one word earlier) instead of 'quotes the beat.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-measured against the current 24-chunk file: every move-entry across chunks 1-21 bolds the full lead sentence (10-17 words), not a short handle, e.g. chunk 5 line 77 bolds 'Names a condition under which the work happens, and names refusal as a valid outcome.' (13 words); chunk 21 line 307 bolds 'Names the moment, quotes the beat. Rules with evidence beat rules without.' (12 words). This file is explicitly a reference/lookup page (`curriculum/trainings/.../reference/`), which the rule's lookup-surface waiver (2026-08-13) exempts from the per-slide ≤1-bold cap — but the waiver text still requires 'bold the label, not the sentence after it,' and this file's own stated contract (line 11, restated in the maintainer block) is to bold the full definition sentence, which the waiver does not cover. Chunks 22-24 (three-move patterns) use italics for the trio-name line, not bold sentences, so they are not flagged. Harm: on a genuinely dense lookup page this dilutes bold from 'here's the handle to scan for' to 'here's a highlighted paragraph,' which is the exact failure the budget exists to prevent — but the shape is uniform and deliberate across all 30 entries, which is evidence of authorial intent rather than an unnoticed default.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Get a maintainer accept-note recording that this reference page's full-sentence-bold shape is a deliberate house style distinct from the waiver's 'bold the label' baseline; otherwise trim each lead to a short handle and unbold the definition clause.
